songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic 46‑min Turn On Your Lovelight with Elvin Bishop guest
ai_show_review.blurb: The show is anchored by a sprawling Turn On Your Lovelight that morphs from tight riffing into a free‑form psychedelic jam. Guest guitarist Elvin Bishop adds blues‑heavy firepower, while the band rides a loose, drug‑induced groove. Smokestack Lightning and Beat It On Down The Line also stand out.
ai_show_review.review: On June 6, 1969 at the Fillmore West the Dead delivered a single‑disc set that revolved around an astonishing ~46‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight. With Elvin Bishop sitting in on guitar, the jam builds from a solid blues riff into a swirling, psychedelic excursion that feels both loose and purposeful – a true snapshot of the band’s drug‑fueled explorations of the era. The audience tape captures decent mids and clear guitar presence despite typical vintage hiss and a splice around 33:25; listeners note occasional level swings but overall it conveys the raw energy of that night. Highlights include a gritty Smokestack Lightning, an upbeat Beat It On Down The Line, and the extended Lovelight that showcases Bishop’s fiery soloing alongside Jerry’s intermittent, yet when present, soaring tone. Phil’s bass is described as less driven, reflecting his heavy dosing, while the rest of the rhythm section keeps the groove steady. For Deadheads interested in a deep dive into early psychedelic jamming with a blues guest star, this recording offers an authentic, if imperfect, listening experience.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality audience tape that captures the full ~46‑minute Lovelight with Elvin Bishop, offering solid mids and clear guitar despite vintage tape hiss.

band_performance.Jerry: Mixed presence – some listeners note he arrives late or is absent on parts of Lovelight, but his tone shines when he does play.
band_performance.Phil: Heavily dosed; bass sounds less driven and reflects the chaotic night described in his book.
